backlog.spec: Supply jac for the objective (gradient: zeros for centres, -1 for radii) and a vectorized analytic Jacobian for the constraint function (pairwise distance rows, wall rows, and r>=0 rows). This removes finite-difference cost (about 78 evals per gradient) and gives many more restarts and converged solves in 30 s. Pass jac=... to minimize.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Once analytic Jacobians exist, set MAX_ITER=500 (or 1000) so SLSQP converges fully instead of stopping at 200. Check that the converged solutions are better per restart.
backlog.title: Raise MAX_ITER to 500 with analytic jac

backlog.spec: Initialize centres from a jittered hexagonal/staggered grid, e.g. rows of 5,5,6,5,5 or 6,5,5,5,5, plus gaussian noise sd 0.03, instead of uniform random. Use the rng to pick the row layout and noise. Start radii at 0.08.
backlog.title: Hex-like structured initialization

backlog.spec: After about 30% of the time spent on random restarts, switch to perturbing the best solution: move 2-3 random circles to random positions, or jitter all centres by sd 0.02, then re-run SLSQP and keep the result if it is better. Use the remaining time for this.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the best solution

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, swap the positions of a large circle and a small circle (or two circles with different radii), reset radii to the mean value, and re-optimize with SLSQP. This explores the combinatorial arrangements.
backlog.title: Swap-radii perturbation

backlog.spec: After the SLSQP run, fix the centres and solve an LP for the radii (maximize the sum of r subject to r_i+r_j<=d_ij, r_i<=wall distance) using scipy.optimize.linprog (highs). The result is exactly feasible and optimal for those centres. Then subtract 1e-12 and verify the packing.
backlog.title: Better repair: LP radii refit

backlog.spec: Reduce SHRINK from 1e-9 to 1e-11, since the tolerance is 1e-10. Keep the final validity check, and fall back to a larger shrink if the check fails.
backlog.title: Smaller SHRINK

backlog.spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.9 and stop starting a new restart if the projected time would exceed the limit, based on the measured duration of the last restart. Use process_time.
backlog.title: Use full time fraction

backlog.spec: Set INIT_RADIUS to 0.03, and test 0.08 as well. The start affects which basins SLSQP finds.
backlog.title: Smaller initial radii

backlog.spec: Set INIT_LOW to 0.03 so initial centres cover the whole square, including near the edges where circles settle.
backlog.title: Wider INIT_LOW range

backlog.spec: First run a cheap stage: L-BFGS-B on a penalty energy (overlap squared plus wall violation squared minus a small weight times the radius sum) from the random start. Then polish with SLSQP. This gives better starts and a lower SLSQP failure rate.
backlog.title: Two-stage optimization with penalty warmup

backlog.spec: In the polishing runs, include only pairs with centre distance below 0.4 in the constraints (recomputed once after a first short SLSQP). This cuts constraints from 325 to about 100 and speeds up each iteration. Verify validity with the full check afterwards.
backlog.title: Sparse neighbor constraints

backlog.spec: After SLSQP on the best candidate, polish with scipy trust-constr using the analytic Jacobian, or SLSQP again with ftol=1e-15 and a high maxiter, then LP refit the radii.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish

backlog.spec: Set options ftol=1e-10 for the final polish of the top candidates and ftol=1e-6 for the screening runs. Screen many starts cheaply, then polish the top 3.
backlog.title: SLSQP ftol tuning

backlog.spec: Run each restart with maxiter=60 and record the sum of radii. Keep a list of the top K=5 candidates, and in the final 40% of the time fully polish them with maxiter=500. Return the best result.
backlog.title: Screen then polish scheme

backlog.spec: Initialize with a mirror-symmetric configuration (13 circles on one half reflected across the diagonal or the vertical axis, with the circles on the axis handled separately) plus small noise. The best known packings are near-symmetric. SLSQP is then free to break the symmetry.
backlog.title: Symmetric starts

backlog.spec: Draw initial radii from uniform(0.04, 0.12) instead of a constant, so the optimizer starts with a mix of big and small circles, as the optimum has.
backlog.title: Radii-diverse initialization

backlog.spec: Generate the initial centres by best-candidate sampling (Mitchell's algorithm): for each new point, pick the farthest from existing points among 10 random candidates. The starts are spread evenly, so there are fewer wasted restarts.
backlog.title: Lloyd/Poisson-disc initial centres

backlog.spec: In the improvement phase, delete the circle with the smallest radius from the best solution. Reinsert it at the largest empty hole (the point maximizing the distance to the others and the walls, found via a random-sample grid of 2000 points), then re-run SLSQP.
backlog.title: Remove smallest and reinsert

backlog.spec: Replace the 50-iteration worst-pair repair with a loop that runs until there is no overlap above 0 (up to 1000 iterations). This avoids a leftover invalid packing and guarantees validity. Combine with the LP refit as a fallback.
backlog.title: Simple repair vectorized and with more iterations

backlog.spec: Use squared-distance constraints, (dx^2+dy^2)-(ri+rj)^2 >= 0, in SLSQP. They are smooth at zero distance, and their Jacobian is cheaper. Keep the final validity check exact.
backlog.title: Constraint scaling

backlog.spec: Run SLSQP with maxiter=40 first. If the resulting sum of radii is below 0.97 times the best so far, discard it. Otherwise continue with the full iteration budget from that point.
backlog.title: Early-abort of bad restarts

backlog.spec: In the local-search phase, perturb the best solution with gaussian noise to the centres whose sd decays from 0.05 to 0.005 over the remaining time. Reset radii to 0.8 times the current ones and re-optimize with SLSQP.
backlog.title: Annealed jitter perturbation

backlog.spec: Keep a pool of the 4 best distinct solutions. Each iteration, choose one at random, perturb it, re-optimize, and replace the worst in the pool if the result is better. This keeps diversity.
backlog.title: Fixed-count local search from top-k pool

backlog.spec: Optimize 27 circles, then drop the smallest. Or optimize 25 and add one circle at the biggest hole. Re-optimize with SLSQP for 26. This gives different basins.
backlog.title: Warm-start from a 25 or 27 circle solution

backlog.spec: Place about 12 circles near the border (a perimeter ring with jitter) and the rest in the interior at random. Optimal packings have many circles touching the walls.
backlog.title: Border-biased initialization

backlog.spec: Give SLSQP explicit bounds: centres in [0,1] and radii in [0,0.25]. This stops runaway variables and removes the wall and r>=0 constraint rows (c-r>=0 stays). The system gets smaller and more stable.
backlog.title: Reduced variable bounds

backlog.spec: After the random initialization, sort the centres by x coordinate and give larger initial radii to the interior circles (radius proportional to the distance from the wall). This regularizes the start so SLSQP converges faster.
backlog.title: Lower-triangle ordering sort

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, grow all radii uniformly from the random centres to the largest feasible common value, scaled by 0.9, so the starting point is feasible. SLSQP then works from feasibility, with fewer infeasible iterations.
backlog.title: Multiple-radius growth start

backlog.spec: Split time: first 40% of the budget runs random-restart SLSQP as now to find the best packing. Then loop until 80% of time: copy the best (c, r), pick 1-3 random circles (bias toward the smallest radii), relocate them to random positions with radius 0.02, add Gaussian jitter (sd 0.01) to all centres, run SLSQP (MAX_ITER 200) from this start, repair, and accept if the sum of radii improves. Keep the best throughout.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from best with local perturbation

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random init by structured starts. Pick a random row pattern for 26 circles, e.g. rows of counts like 5,5,5,5,6 or 6,5,6,5,4 (randomly choose from a few patterns summing to 26). Place centres evenly in each row, with rows evenly spaced in y and with alternate rows offset in x. Add jitter of sd 0.02 and set initial radii to 0.07. Use these in every restart, with the pattern and jitter drawn from rng.
backlog.title: Hex/grid structured starts with jitter

backlog.spec: Replace _repair's iterative shrinking with an exact LP. Given the centres, maximise sum(r) subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij, r_i <= wall distance, r >= 0, using scipy.optimize.linprog (highs). Subtract 1e-12 from the radii, then run a final check that shrinks any residual violation. This recovers the radius mass lost by the greedy shrink, and the LP is cheap enough to run on every restart.
backlog.title: LP radius refit after SLSQP

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP run, polish with a few alternations. (a) Solve the LP for the optimal radii given the centres. (b) Take the active contacts (gap < 1e-6) and run SLSQP on all variables, keeping only the near-pair constraints (d < r_i + r_j + 0.05) from the current state, with maxiter 100. Repeat 3 times and keep the best valid result. This is meant to converge to a tight local optimum.
backlog.title: Alternate LP radii and centre-gradient steps

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run 100 steps of a cheap vectorized gradient-style relaxation on the centres and radii. The objective is -sum(r) + mu * sum(max(0, overlap)^2) plus the wall violations, with mu growing from 1 to 1000 and step size 0.01. Use plain numpy with analytic gradients. Then hand this state to SLSQP with maxiter 150. Starting near feasibility should make each SLSQP run converge to better optima.
backlog.title: Penalty-based warmup then SLSQP

backlog.spec: After the initial restarts (40% of the time), run a local search. Take the best solution, delete the circle with the smallest radius, and find the largest hole by sampling 20000 random points and taking the point that maximises min(distance to the other circles' edges, wall distance). Reinsert the circle there with that radius. Then run SLSQP with maxiter 200 and accept if the sum improves. Also try the second-smallest circle on later iterations.
backlog.title: Remove-smallest-and-reinsert moves

backlog.spec: Pick n+1 or n-1 randomly. Run a short SLSQP (maxiter 150) for that count from random starts. Then convert it to n circles by dropping the smallest circle (for 27) or inserting a circle at the largest hole with a small radius (for 25). Finish with a full SLSQP (maxiter 200) for n. Use this as an alternative start type, half of the restarts.
backlog.title: Warm start from a 25 or 27 circle solution

backlog.spec: Generate initial centres for n//2=13 circles uniformly in the left half x in [0.05, 0.5]. Mirror them to x -> 1-x. For odd n (26 is even, but keep the code general), add an extra circle on the axis x=0.5. Add small jitter of sd 0.005 to break the exact symmetry. Run unconstrained SLSQP from there. Many good packings are near-symmetric, so this may raise the hit rate. Alternate symmetric and random starts.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric starts

backlog.spec: Run each restart in two stages. Stage 1 is SLSQP with maxiter 60. Keep a running list of stage-1 sums. Only continue to stage 2 (maxiter 250, warm start from the stage-1 result) if the stage-1 sum is above the median of the previous stage-1 sums, and always for the first 5. This should multiply the number of restarts and focus the time on promising basins.
backlog.title: Shorter SLSQP runs with early pruning

backlog.spec: Give SLSQP explicit bounds: centres in [0,1], radii in [0, 0.25]. Sort the initial circles by radius so the larger initial radii come first. Initialise radii from a spread such as linspace(0.03, 0.12, n) shuffled against the centres. Use a variable scaling that multiplies the radius variables by 5 in the optimizer, so the radii and the centres are on similar scales. Apply the same scaling in the constraints.
backlog.title: Tight bounds and radius-ordered variable scaling

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when start is None, with probability 0.5 build the initial centres from a staggered-row layout: pick a row-count pattern from a few options such as [5,5,5,5,6] or [4,5,4,5,4,4] (summing to 26), place rows evenly in y, place circles evenly in x within each row with alternate rows offset, add gaussian jitter sd 0.02, and set radii to 0.5/ max(row count). Otherwise use the random start. Seeded via rng.
backlog.title: Hex-row structured starts with jitter

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase of solve (after 30% of the time), add a move that takes the best packing, picks the 1-2 circles with the smallest radii, and relocates them to the largest empty spots. Find the spots by evaluating 2000 random points and taking those with the maximum distance-to-nearest-circle-surface, and use a small initial radius of 0.02 there. Then run SLSQP from this start. Choose this move with probability 1/3 among the perturbation types.
backlog.title: Remove-smallest-and-reinsert move

backlog.spec: Change the random-restart share from 0.3 to 0.15 in the solve loop condition (0.3 * TIME_FRACTION * time_limit becomes 0.15 * ...), so more time goes to perturbing the best packing, which was the only thing that helped.
backlog.title: Perturbation share sweep: 15% random then local search

backlog.spec: Keep a list of the 4 best distinct packings (by sum of radii) from the random-restart phase. In the perturbation phase, pick an elite at random (biased to the best, e.g. weights 4,3,2,1) as the start for each perturbation, and replace the worst elite if the new result beats it and its sum differs by more than 1e-6 from all others. Return the overall best.
backlog.title: Pool of top-4 elites for perturbation

backlog.spec: Add a perturbation move: choose two circles with noticeably different radii (ratio > 1.3), swap their centres, set both radii to the smaller of the two times 0.8, and re-run SLSQP. Use it with probability 0.3 in the perturbation phase, in addition to the existing moves.
backlog.title: Swap two circles of different radii

backlog.spec: For a random start with probability 0.3, generate 13 random centres in the left half (x in [0.05,0.5]) and mirror them to x -> 1-x, giving 26 circles, with radius 0.05 and tiny jitter 1e-3 to break exact symmetry. SLSQP then runs from this symmetric start. Other starts remain unchanged.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric starts

backlog.spec: Replace the random start with a start from farthest-point sampling: generate 400 random candidate points in the square, pick the first at random, then repeatedly choose the candidate maximizing min(distance to chosen centres, distance to walls*2). Set the initial radii to half the distance to the nearest neighbour or wall, capped at 0.12. This gives well-spread centres with varied radii. Use it for half of the random restarts.
backlog.title: Greedy radius-growth start (maximin centres)

backlog.spec: In the random-restart phase run SLSQP first with maxiter=40, repair and compute the sum. Continue with another maxiter=160 run from that point only if the sum is within 0.03 of the best sum seen so far (or if there is no best). This saves time on bad basins and gives more restarts. Keep the final repair as it is.
backlog.title: Early-abort bad restarts with short SLSQP stage

backlog.spec: Scale the objective by 10 (minimize -10*sum r, with gradient scaling) so that SLSQP's line search treats the objective better against the constraint violation, and keep tolerance ftol=1e-9 default. Compare against the current performance. Only the objective lambda changes: lambda v: -10*v[2*n:].sum().
backlog.title: Constraint scaling by weighting wall and radius terms

backlog.spec: In the perturbation branch that adds gaussian noise (sd 0.02), draw the noise sd per call from a log-uniform on [0.005, 0.06], and in the move-circles branch draw k from 1 to 5. Also shrink all radii by 10% in the start vector so that SLSQP begins from a feasible, slightly loose configuration.
backlog.title: Two-step perturbation: shake with bigger noise then polish

backlog.spec: Combine the two best findings. In _solve_once for fresh random starts run SLSQP with maxiter=40 first, then continue from that result with maxiter=160 (a second minimize call from res.x). Keep the slot 7 schedule: random restarts for the first 30% of the TIME_FRACTION budget, then perturb the best packing (move 2-3 circles or add jitter). Use the two-stage solve in both phases. This is a replicate-and-combine test.
backlog.title: Two-stage SLSQP plus 30% restart perturbation search

backlog.spec: For half of the random restarts build the initial centres from a hex-like layout. Choose row counts from a random pattern such as [5,5,5,5,6] or [4,5,4,5,4,4] summing to 26, place circles evenly along each row with alternate rows offset by half a spacing, rows evenly spaced in y, and add gaussian jitter sd 0.02. Use the initial radius 0.05 and clip centres to [0.05, 0.95]. The other half stay uniform random. Draw the pattern from the seeded rng.
backlog.title: Hex-row structured starts with jitter

backlog.spec: After 30% of the time, keep a pool of the 4 best distinct packings by sum of radii. Each iteration pick a random elite, perturb it (move 2-3 circles to random places or jitter sd 0.02), run SLSQP, repair, and insert the result into the pool if it beats the worst member. This replaces the single-best perturbation, so the search does not get stuck on one basin.
backlog.title: Accept-if-better basin hopping with a pool of 4 elites

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase add a move: pick two circles whose radii differ by at least 0.03, exchange their centres, set both radii to the mean of the two, then run SLSQP. Use this for a third of the perturbations, alongside the existing moves.
backlog.title: Swap a large and a small circle then re-optimize

backlog.spec: Multiply the pair constraints and the wall constraints by 10 in cons, so that the constraint residuals are larger relative to the objective in SLSQP's line search and its feasibility tolerance. Keep the radius positivity constraint unscaled. The feasible set stays the same. Repair still runs after the solve.
backlog.title: Constraint scaling for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Build initial centres by farthest-point sampling. Draw 200 random candidate points in the unit square, then pick 26 one at a time, each maximising the minimum distance to the points already chosen and to the walls. Set each initial radius to 0.45 times the distance to its nearest neighbour or wall. Use this for 30% of the random restarts, with a small jitter of sd 0.01 so the starts differ.
backlog.title: Greedy maximin-start with radius growth

backlog.spec: Known good packings put many circles along the walls and corners. In 50% of the restarts place 12 circles near the border, at distance uniform(0.04, 0.1) from a randomly chosen wall, and the other 14 uniformly in [0.15, 0.85]. Start all radii at 0.05.
backlog.title: Border-biased initial centres

backlog.spec: Run each fresh restart for 30 SLSQP iterations first. Compute the sum of radii and compare it with the best sum so far. Continue with 170 more iterations only if the sum is within 0.05 of the best, or if no best exists yet. Otherwise discard the start. This saves time for more restarts, and ignores the repair step until the end.
backlog.title: Early abort of bad restarts

backlog.spec: Pass bounds to SLSQP: centres in [0, 1] and radii in [0, 0.2]. This keeps the optimizer from wandering to infeasible regions and large radii, and it makes the early iterations more stable. No other change.
backlog.title: Reduced variable bounds

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, with probability 0.3 apply a big move: relocate 4-6 random circles to random positions with radius 0.02, and add gaussian jitter sd 0.03 on all the centres. Then run the two-stage SLSQP. With the other 0.7 probability keep the small moves. Accept the result only if it improves the best.
backlog.title: Perturbation with larger shake then polish

backlog.spec: Keep the slot 7 structure (30% of the time on random restarts, then perturb the best packing by moving 2-3 circles or jittering). Inside _solve_once, run SLSQP in two stages: 40 iterations, then 160 more continuing from the result. In the random-restart phase, make half of the starts mirror-symmetric: draw left-half centres uniformly in x in [INIT_LOW, 0.5], mirror them to 1-x for the other half, and put any odd circle on x=0.5. Keep the rest unchanged.
backlog.title: Combine perturbation search, two-stage SLSQP and symmetric starts

backlog.spec: Change the switch point from 0.3*TIME_FRACTION*time_limit to 0.15*TIME_FRACTION*time_limit, so the remaining time goes to perturbation of the best packing. Nothing else changes. This tests whether more local search helps.
backlog.title: Restart share 15% before perturbation search

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, track the current packing separately from the best. Perturb the current one, and accept the result if its sum of radii is at least current minus 0.002 (a small tolerance). Keep the global best separately. If there are 40 consecutive non-improving steps, reset the current packing to the best packing with a larger shake (move 4 circles).
backlog.title: Accept-if-better basin hopping with a stuck restart

backlog.spec: For random restarts, run SLSQP for 30 iterations first. Compute the sum of radii from the result. If it is below the best sum of the current run minus 0.05, skip the rest and do not repair it. Otherwise continue with 170 more iterations from that point. This saves time for more restarts.
backlog.title: Early-abort bad restarts with a short SLSQP stage

backlog.spec: Build random-restart starts like this. Sample 400 candidate points in the unit square. Pick n of them greedily so that each new point is the farthest from the already chosen ones and from the walls (maximin with a random first point). Set the initial radius of each point to 0.4 times its nearest-neighbour or wall distance. Use these as x0 for SLSQP in half of the restarts.
backlog.title: Greedy maximin start with radius growth

backlog.spec: Multiply the objective by 10 (minimise -10*sum r) so that SLSQP takes better steps. Keep the constraint functions unchanged. Also add variable bounds: centres in [0,1] and radii in [0,0.5]. This changes the conditioning only and the final result is still repaired as before.
backlog.title: Scale constraints so walls and pairs are comparable

backlog.spec: In half of the restarts in the perturbation phase, take the best packing and remove the circle with the smallest radius. Re-insert it at the centre of the largest hole. Find the hole by evaluating 2000 random points and picking the one with the largest minimum of (distance to the nearest centre minus its radius) and the wall distance. Set its radius to 0.5 times that margin and run SLSQP.
backlog.title: Warm start from 25-circle solution plus 1 new circle

backlog.spec: Initialise random-restart starts from rows of circles: pick a random number of rows from 4 to 6, split n circles among rows as evenly as possible with a random permutation of the extra counts, place each row at evenly spaced y and the circles at evenly spaced x with a random half-spacing offset on alternate rows. Add jitter of sd 0.02 and use radius 0.05. Use this for 50% of the restarts.
backlog.title: Hex-row starts with random row counts

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, apply a larger shake (sd 0.05 noise on all centres), run a short SLSQP of 60 iterations, then compare with the best. Only if the result is within 0.02 of the best sum, run another 150 iterations of SLSQP. This focuses effort on promising basins.
backlog.title: Ensemble of larger-shake perturbations then polish by radius-only LP

backlog.spec: In solve(), change the threshold for switching from fresh random restarts to perturbation of the best packing from 0.3*TIME_FRACTION*time_limit to 0.15*TIME_FRACTION*time_limit. Keep everything else from the current code unchanged. Slot 7 suggested a smaller restart share is better.
backlog.title: Restart share 15% then perturbation search

backlog.spec: Keep the 30% restart / perturbation structure. In _solve_once, run SLSQP first with maxiter=40, then restart SLSQP from its result with maxiter=160 (and the same constraints). Use the two-stage for every call, both fresh and perturbed starts. Do not change anything else.
backlog.title: Combine two-stage SLSQP with perturbation search

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts, generate centres by best-candidate sampling (Mitchell): for each of the n points draw 20 random candidates in [0.05,0.95]^2 and keep the one farthest from existing points. Set initial radii to 0.4 times the nearest-neighbour distance (capped by wall distance). Use these as SLSQP x0 in place of uniform centres; perturbation starts remain unchanged.
backlog.title: Greedy maximin start with radius growth

backlog.spec: In the fresh restart phase, run SLSQP with maxiter=30 first and compute the sum of radii. Only continue with maxiter=170 more iterations from that point if the sum is at least the 60th percentile of the previous first-stage sums, or if fewer than 5 were recorded. Otherwise discard and move on. Track first-stage sums in a list inside solve().
backlog.title: Early abort of bad restarts via short SLSQP stage

backlog.spec: Multiply the pair-distance constraints by 1/(2*0.1)=5 and keep wall and radius constraints unscaled, or equivalently scale all constraint values so that gradients have similar magnitude. Pass the scaled cons function to SLSQP. The repair step is unchanged, so validity is still guaranteed.
backlog.title: Constraint scaling in SLSQP

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, for a third of perturbations: delete the smallest circle, then place it at the point of a 40x40 grid with the maximal distance to the surrounding circle edges and walls (max of min(dist to centres minus radii, wall distance)), with initial radius 0.5 times that clearance. Then run SLSQP as usual. Keep the existing perturbations for the other two thirds.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert at the largest hole

backlog.spec: After SLSQP on each candidate, run 5 rounds of: solve the LP maximizing sum of radii for fixed centres (scipy linprog highs, constraints r_i+r_j<=d_ij, r_i<=wall distance), then move centres slightly by a gradient-free step: shift each circle toward the centroid of the free space by 0.1 times its slack. Keep the best packing found and feed it to repair.
backlog.title: Alternate-radius LP and centre moves

backlog.spec: Set INIT_LOW to 0.02 and draw initial radii from a bimodal mix: 6 randomly chosen circles with radius 0.12 and the others with radius 0.07. This addresses the known optimal structure with a few large circles and many smaller ones. Apply to fresh random starts only.
backlog.title: Wider initial region and sizes mix

backlog.spec: Set SHRINK to 1e-11 and, after repair, check validity with the harness criterion (pair distance minus radii sum >= -1e-10 and walls). If any violation exists, subtract 1e-9 from all radii and recheck, in a loop of at most 5 times. This recovers about 2e-8 per circle, a tiny but free gain. Keep it simple.
backlog.title: Smaller SHRINK with exact tolerance repair

backlog.spec: For half of fresh random starts, choose a random partition of 26 into 5 or 6 rows with counts between 3 and 6. Place rows at evenly spaced y values in [0.1,0.9], circles evenly spaced in x with a random half-offset on alternate rows, plus Gaussian jitter sd 0.02. Initial radius 0.06. Other half stay uniform random.
backlog.title: Hex-row starts with random row counts

backlog.spec: Replicate the best-looking data idea together with the incumbent: in fresh random starts (before the perturbation phase), half of starts use farthest-point sampling of centres (choose each next centre from 400 random candidates maximizing min distance to the already chosen ones and to the walls) with initial radius 0.05; the other half stay uniform. Keep the 30% restart share and the existing perturbation phase unchanged. This is a replicate-and-combine step on slot 34, which scored -2.6342/-2.6337.
backlog.title: Combine maximin starts with 30% restart share and perturbation

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, after each SLSQP run, compute the exact optimal radii for the fixed centres by scipy.optimize.linprog (highs): maximize sum r subject to r_i+r_j<=d_ij, r_i<=wall distance, r>=0. Use this only to compare candidates for acceptance, and keep the existing repair for the final answer. This gives a cleaner objective for accepting moves. Skip it for the random-restart phase.
backlog.title: Fixed-centre LP radii then SLSQP polish of the perturbation candidates only

backlog.spec: Replace the fresh random start with a constructive one: sample 300 candidate points, and repeatedly add the point that has the largest possible radius, defined as min(wall distance, distance to the nearest placed circle minus that circle's radius), until 26 circles are placed. Use these centres and radii (floored at 0.01) as the SLSQP start. Do this for 50% of fresh starts, and add noise sd 0.01 to the centres.
backlog.title: Greedy radius-growth start

backlog.spec: Multiply the pair-distance constraints by a factor of 4, and the wall and radius constraints by 1, so that active pair and wall terms have comparable gradient scale. Also scale the objective by 10 (minimize -10*sum r). Leave everything else unchanged. SLSQP's line search and its termination test depend on scale, so this may change convergence on every restart.
backlog.title: Constraint scaling for SLSQP

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, a third of the moves pick a random point in the square and take the 5 to 7 circles nearest to it. Re-place those circles at random positions inside their joint bounding box, with radius 0.03, and keep the other circles fixed at their current centres and radii. Run a short SLSQP (60 iterations) over all variables, then 140 more. Accept the result if the repaired sum improves.
backlog.title: Bolder: large neighbourhood re-solve of a spatial window

backlog.spec: For half of the fresh starts, use point-symmetric centres through (0.5, 0.5): draw 13 random circles and mirror them via c -> 1-c. Set radii equal for each mirror pair. SLSQP will usually break the symmetry slightly, which is fine. The other half stay uniform. This differs from the earlier left-right mirror idea.
backlog.title: Radius-ordered symmetric restart with a point-reflection

backlog.spec: Set INIT_LOW to 0.03 so that the random centres cover almost all of the square, including the near-wall zone. Draw initial radii from a log-uniform range [0.03, 0.12]. Leave the rest of the script unchanged.
backlog.title: Wider INIT_LOW and mixed initial radii

backlog.spec: Reduce SHRINK from 1e-9 to 2e-11. Run the harness check inside _repair: after shrinking, compute the largest overlap and wall violation, and if it exceeds 5e-11 subtract that excess from the radii involved. This should gain about 1e-9 per circle at best, so it is tiny, but it is safe.
backlog.title: Smaller SHRINK with a verified repair

backlog.spec: In half of the fresh starts, first optimize 24 circles with 100 SLSQP iterations, and then insert 2 circles at the two largest holes. Find the holes by sampling 2000 random points and picking those with the largest distance to the nearest circle edge, with a minimum separation between the two picks of 0.1. Give the new circles radius 0.02, and run the full SLSQP on all 26.
backlog.title: Bolder: random-restart then SLSQP from a 25-circle optimum plus two inserts

backlog.spec: Make slot 34 the base: half of fresh random starts use farthest-point (maximin) sampled centres from 400 candidates with initial radius 0.05. In the perturbation phase (after 30% of time), additionally use slot 31's move for half of the perturbations: add normal noise sd 0.05 to all centres of the best packing, run SLSQP with maxiter=60, then continue with the normal 200-iteration SLSQP, and keep it only if the repaired sum improves. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Maximin starts + shake-all perturbation combined

backlog.spec: Use the slot 34 maximin start for half of fresh starts and the original single-circle-move perturbation phase, but change the restart share from 0.3 to 0.2 of the budget. This tests whether a shorter random phase pays off when starts are better. Change only the share constant and the start generator.
backlog.title: Maximin starts, restart share 20%

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, pick a random point in the square. Pick the 6-8 circles nearest to it. Re-initialise those circles to random centres inside their bounding box, with radius 0.03. Keep the other circles fixed at the best packing's values, and run SLSQP on all variables for 200 iterations. Accept the result if the repaired sum improves. Use this for half of the perturbations in place of the 2-3 circle move.
backlog.title: Window re-solve (large neighbourhood)

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP in the perturbation phase, run 3 rounds of: (a) solve the LP for the radii with the centres fixed, using scipy linprog highs, maximising the sum of radii under pair and wall constraints; (b) a short SLSQP of 30 iterations on all variables from that point. Keep the best valid result. Apply this only to candidates whose first-stage sum is within 0.003 of the best.
backlog.title: Alternate LP radii and centre steps

backlog.spec: Run every fresh restart for 30 SLSQP iterations first. Compute the repaired sum, and continue to 200 iterations only if it is at least 0.02 below the best-so-far sum or no best exists. Otherwise discard it. This frees time for more starts in the 30% restart phase. Use the existing options dict with a warm start from res.x.
backlog.title: Early abort of poor restarts

backlog.spec: New perturbation move, used with probability 1/4. Remove the circle with the smallest radius. Sample 2000 random points and take the one with the largest distance-to-nearest-circle-edge (min over j of d minus r_j, and wall distance). Put the circle there with radius equal to that clearance. Then run the normal SLSQP. Accept if the repaired sum improves.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert at the largest hole

backlog.spec: Pass bounds to SLSQP: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.2]. Reduce SHRINK to 1e-11. After repair, verify the exact pairwise check in double precision. If it fails, fall back to SHRINK=1e-9. This tests whether the shrink loss matters and keeps the variables in range.
backlog.title: Bounded variables and tight SHRINK

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts choose one of three init types with equal probability: uniform random, farthest-point maximin centres from 400 candidates, and jittered staggered rows (5 or 6 rows with random row counts summing to 26, jitter sd 0.02). Perturbation phase and the rest stay as in the incumbent.
backlog.title: Maximin starts plus staggered-row starts mixture

backlog.spec: In the restart phase, run each fresh start for 30 SLSQP iterations first and compute the repaired sum of radii. If it is below the 60th percentile of the first-stage sums seen so far (once at least 5 have been seen), discard it. Otherwise continue with 170 more iterations from that point. This spends more of the budget on promising basins. Keep the 30% restart / perturbation split.
backlog.title: Early-abort restarts via short SLSQP stage

backlog.spec: Multiply the pair-distance constraints by 1/(1+...) is not needed. Instead scale the wall constraints and the r>=0 constraints by a factor of 2 and the pair constraints by 1, and scale the objective by 10 (minimise -10*sum r). The aim is a better-conditioned SLSQP QP subproblem. Change nothing else and keep the validity repair.
backlog.title: Constraint scaling for SLSQP

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP run in the perturbation phase only, run 3 rounds of: fix the centres and solve the radii LP exactly with scipy linprog (highs; constraints r_i+r_j<=d_ij, r_i<=wall distance), then run SLSQP for 25 iterations from the LP solution. Keep the best repaired result. This differs from slot 5, which used one LP refit in the restart phase.
backlog.title: Alternate LP radii and centre steps

backlog.spec: For some fresh starts, solve 24 circles with SLSQP (150 iterations) from a random start. Insert 2 new circles at the two largest holes (found by random point sampling) with radius 0.02, then run the full 26-circle SLSQP. Use this for 40% of the fresh starts in the restart phase and keep the incumbent perturbation phase.
backlog.title: Warm start from a 25-circle optimum plus two inserts

backlog.spec: Draw initial centres uniform in [0.03, 0.97] instead of INIT_LOW 0.1. Draw initial radii from a log-uniform range of [0.02, 0.14], sorted so that larger radii are assigned to centres nearer the middle. Keep the rest unchanged.
backlog.title: Wider initial region mixed radii

backlog.spec: Set SHRINK to 1e-12 and after the repair loop run an exact check. Compute max overlap and wall violation in double precision. If any violation exceeds 5e-11, shrink all radii by a further 2e-11 and recheck, up to 5 times. This gains about 26e-9 per run, which is tiny but free. Repair iterations rise from 50 to 200.
backlog.title: Smaller SHRINK with verified exact repair

backlog.spec: Pass bounds to SLSQP: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.2]. Radius-ordered scaling is not needed. Combine this with a perturbation phase that jitters only the 8 circles with the smallest radii, with sd 0.04, and then polishes everything. Replicate the result because single runs are noisy.
backlog.title: Bounded variables with radius cap

backlog.spec: Combine two partly accepted ideas. Half of fresh random starts use jittered staggered rows: pick 5 rows, with counts from a random permutation of [5,5,6,5,5], x positions evenly spaced with a random offset, jitter sd 0.02, initial radius 0.05. In the perturbation phase (after 30% of the budget), half of the perturbations re-initialise the 6-8 circles nearest a random point at random positions inside that disc, with radius 0.03, then run SLSQP on all circles. Keep the best-so-far logic unchanged. Replicate the result.
backlog.title: Staggered-row starts plus window re-solve combined

backlog.spec: Half of fresh random starts use farthest-point sampling: draw 400 uniform candidates in [0.03,0.97]^2, pick the first at random, then repeatedly add the candidate with the largest min distance to those already chosen until n are picked. Use initial radius 0.05. In the perturbation phase, every perturbation shakes all centres with Gaussian sd 0.05, clips to [0.01,0.99], and runs SLSQP with MAX_ITER=60 from the shaken state, with radii set to 0.8 times the current radii. Accept only if the repaired sum is better than the best.
backlog.title: Maximin starts plus shake-all perturbation

backlog.spec: New perturbation move for 1/3 of perturbations. Remove the 1-2 smallest-radius circles from the best packing. Estimate the largest empty hole with 2000 random points in the square, and keep the point that maximises the min over circles of (distance to centre minus radius) and the wall distance. Put the removed circles at that point, or at the second-best point if it is at least 0.1 away, with radius 0.02. Then run SLSQP on all circles and keep the result if it is better.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert at the largest hole

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP result and before the repair, run 3 rounds of this refinement. First, fix the centres and solve the radii exactly with scipy linprog (highs): maximise sum r subject to r_i+r_j<=d_ij, r_i<=wall distance, r>=0. Then nudge the centres by a small SLSQP run of 30 iterations from the LP radii. Keep the final result if the repaired sum improves. Apply it only to the perturbation-phase candidates that are within 0.01 of the best sum, so it costs little time.
backlog.title: Alternating LP radii and centre steps

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts, run SLSQP with maxiter=30 first. Compute the repaired sum, and abandon the start if it is below the median of the previous restarts' 30-iteration sums minus 0.02, once at least 5 have been recorded. Otherwise continue with 170 more iterations from the current x. Record the 30-iteration sums in a list. This should increase the number of explored starts in the restart phase.
backlog.title: Early abort on weak restarts

backlog.spec: Lower SHRINK from 1e-9 to 2e-11. After repair, verify exactly: compute the min of (d_ij - r_i - r_j) over pairs and the wall slacks in double precision. If any is below -1e-11, subtract the violation from the radii involved, or apply a global shrink of 1e-10, and loop until valid. This keeps the packing inside the harness tolerance of 1e-10 while recovering about 26*1e-9 of sum, and it removes one source of loss.
backlog.title: Smaller SHRINK with verified repair

backlog.spec: Set INIT_LOW to 0.03 so initial centres are uniform in [0.03,0.97]. Draw initial radii from a log-uniform mixture, 0.02 to 0.14 per circle, sorted at random. Apply this to fresh starts only. Leave the perturbation phase untouched. Replicate the result at least twice, because of the noise sd of 0.0023.
backlog.title: Wider initial region with mixed radii

backlog.spec: Set the restart share to 20% instead of 30% of the budget. In the perturbation phase, keep two incumbents. The first is the global best. The second is the best from a fresh random start made after the 20% mark. Alternate perturbation rounds between them. Every 25 rounds, replace the second incumbent with a new fresh-start result if the second one has not improved. Use shake sd 0.05, 60 SLSQP iterations, and accept only on improvement, as in the shake scheme.
backlog.title: Two-population restart with hybrid share tuning

backlog.spec: Make half of fresh random starts use farthest-point maximin centres: for each start, pick the first centre uniformly in [0.05,0.95]^2 and then repeatedly add the candidate (out of 300 uniform random points per step) with the largest minimum distance to the chosen centres and to the walls. Initial radii 0.05. Set the restart share to 20% of the time budget (replace 0.3 in the perturbation switch) and keep the existing perturbation phase. This combines the replicated winners (slots 34 and 61) into one base.
backlog.title: Maximin starts as base with 20% restart share

backlog.spec: For fresh starts choose uniformly among three generators: uniform random centres, farthest-point maximin centres (200 candidates), and jittered staggered rows (5 or 6 rows with row counts summing to 26, alternate rows offset by half a spacing, jitter sd 0.02). Keep the existing perturbation phase at 25% restart share. Replicate-friendly combination of slots 41 and 34.
backlog.title: Staggered-row starts plus maximin mix

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase alternate three moves by random choice: (a) window re-solve (re-initialise the 6-8 circles nearest a random point at random positions with radius 0.03, then SLSQP all), (b) shake all centres with sd 0.05 then 60-iteration SLSQP followed by full SLSQP, (c) existing 2-3 circle relocation. Accept only if sum of repaired radii improves. Combines slots 45 and 31.
backlog.title: Window re-solve with shake-all alternation

backlog.spec: For 40% of fresh starts: solve 24 circles with SLSQP (150 iterations), then insert 2 circles at the two largest voids found by evaluating 2000 random points for max clearance (distance to nearest circle edge and walls), with radius 0.5x the clearance, then run the full 26-circle SLSQP. Include this as another generator in the restart phase with a 25% restart share.
backlog.title: Remove-smallest and re-run with 25-circle optimum plus two inserts

backlog.spec: Replace the pair constraint sqrt(dist2) - ri - rj with a smooth form: dist2 - (ri+rj)^2, divided by 4 (scaled so gradients are O(1)), and keep wall constraints unchanged. This removes the sqrt non-smoothness at zero distance and may change SLSQP convergence. Keep the final repair identical so validity is guaranteed.
backlog.title: Constraint scaling with squared-distance pair constraints

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, add a move with probability 0.3: remove the smallest circle, evaluate 3000 random points for max clearance to the remaining circles (distance minus radius) and walls, place the circle at the best point with radius 0.5x the clearance, then SLSQP 200 iterations. Combine with the 25% restart share and existing moves. Replicate twice.
backlog.title: Hole-guided relocation of the smallest circle

backlog.spec: Keep a pool of the 6 best distinct packings from the restart phase (distinct if sum of radii differs by more than 1e-4). In the second phase, with probability 0.4 create a child by taking circles with centre x<t from parent A and x>=t from parent B (t uniform in 0.35-0.65), fix the count to 26 by dropping the smallest extras or adding random circles of radius 0.03, then SLSQP and repair. Else perform the usual perturbation of the best. Insert children into the pool if they beat the worst.
backlog.title: Population with crossover of halves

backlog.spec: Set SHRINK to 1e-11 and replace the repair with a loop: after shrinking, verify exactly in double precision that every pair has d >= ri+rj-1e-10 and every wall holds; if not, scale all radii by (1-1e-9) and recheck up to 5 times. This recovers up to about 26e-9 per run, which is tiny, so use it as a free add-on to any accepted base. It must never produce an invalid packing.
backlog.title: Lower SHRINK with verified repair

backlog.spec: For fresh starts draw centres uniform in [0.03,0.97], with initial radii drawn from a two-class mix: 8 circles at 0.11 and 18 at 0.05, shuffled. Combine with maximin positions for the big circles (farthest-point from 100 candidates) and uniform random for the small ones. Use 25% restart share. Replicate twice.
backlog.title: Bigger initial region and varied radii mix for fresh starts

backlog.spec: Combine the best-replicated base: half of fresh starts use jittered staggered rows (5 rows, row counts a random permutation of [5,5,6,5,5], x jitter sd 0.03, radii init 0.05) and half use uniform random. Set the restart share to 20% of the budget (replace the 0.3 factor) before the perturbation phase. Keep the rest unchanged. This is a clean base to replicate.
backlog.title: Staggered-row base plus 20% restart share

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase only, build SLSQP constraints from pairs whose centre distance in the starting point is below r_i+r_j+0.25, plus the wall and radius constraints. After the solve, check all pairs. If a violation exceeds 1e-9, rerun with the full constraint set. This makes each local solve several times faster, so many more perturbations fit in the budget.
backlog.title: Sparse neighbour-list constraints in the perturbation phase

backlog.spec: Write the constraint function and its dense Jacobian with numpy (pair rows via the iu index arrays, using np.add.at-free fancy assignment). Pass jac= to SLSQP only for the perturbation-phase solves and the objective gradient (-1 on radii). Keep restart-phase code as is. The aim is more perturbation iterations per second without changing the search.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobian with vectorized sparse pairs, used only in perturbation phase

backlog.spec: In the restart phase, launch 12 starts, run each for 25 SLSQP iterations, and keep the best 4 by sum of radii minus a penalty of 5*max violation. Continue those 4 for 175 more iterations by calling minimize again from the current x. Repeat with fresh batches until the restart share ends. Then run the perturbation phase from the best.
backlog.title: Time-sliced successive halving of restarts

backlog.spec: Maintain the current packing and the best packing separately. Perturb the current one (move 1-3 circles or jitter) and re-solve. Accept the result if it is better, or with probability exp((new-cur)/T). T decays geometrically from 0.004 to 0.0003 over the phase. Return the best seen. This lets the search leave local optima instead of always restarting from the best.
backlog.title: Simulated-annealing acceptance in the perturbation phase

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, solve a sequence of SLSQP problems that maximize sum(r) with radii upper bounds cap = 0.06, 0.09, 0.13 (via bounds), 40 iterations each, warm-started from the previous result, then a final 100 iterations with no cap. The cap prevents early large circles from locking in a bad topology. Use for half of fresh starts.
backlog.title: Radius-growth penalty continuation

backlog.spec: For half of fresh starts, sample 26 centres by Mitchell best-candidate, then apply 5 Lloyd iterations using a 60x60 grid of sample points assigned to the nearest centre (move each centre to its cell centroid). Set initial radii to 0.4 times the nearest-neighbour distance, then run SLSQP. This gives uniform-density starts. Use the other half as uniform random.
backlog.title: Lloyd-relaxed Poisson-disc starts with size-graded radii

backlog.spec: Perturbation move: pick a random subset of 8-10 circles. Fix the other circles' centres through narrow bounds (±1e-4) for a first 40-iteration SLSQP, so only the subset and all radii move. Then release all bounds and polish with 100 iterations. This is a block-coordinate large-neighbourhood search that does not use a spatial window.
backlog.title: Corner and edge circle fixing in the perturbation phase

backlog.spec: Keep the 4 best distinct packings. Create a child by taking circles from parent A with x<t (t uniform in [0.35,0.65]) and from parent B with x>=t. Remove or add circles by size rank so the total is n: if too many, drop the smallest radii. If too few, add circles at the largest empty spots, found from random candidate points and maximum distance to the circle edges. Shrink radii to 0.8x, then run SLSQP. Use this for 30% of the perturbation phase.
backlog.title: Two-parent crossover of packings

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase use a single move type that perturbs all circles: centres get gaussian noise with sd drawn as 0.08*(1-progress)+0.01, where progress is the fraction of the phase elapsed. Radii are multiplied by 0.7, and 80 SLSQP iterations are followed by 120 more only if the first stage result is within 0.01 of the best. Accept if better.
backlog.title: Per-process mixed-seed multi-start of hybrid perturbation with decreasing radius jitter

incumbent.description: After 30% of the time on random restarts, perturb the best packing (move 2-3 circles or jitter all centres by sd 0.02), re-run SLSQP and keep improvements.

memo:
Helped: only slot 7 was accepted (30% of time on random restarts, then perturbing the best packing), at -2.6310/-2.6316. Single runs are noisy (sd about 0.0023), so many single-run rejections may be unreliable.

Did not help: small tweaks to init radii (0, 2), analytic gradients (3), screening or looser tolerances (1, 10), LP refit (5), TIME_FRACTION 0.9 (9), MAX_ITER 500 (12), final polish (13), elite pools (19, 72), and small perturbation variants (22, 25, 26, 28). SLSQP bounds (56) were worse.

Promising: structured or diverse starts and bigger moves. Slot 61 (-2.6360/-2.6334), slot 45 (-2.6354/-2.6334), slot 50 (-2.6349/-2.6331), slot 69 (-2.6343/-2.6349), and slots 34, 41, 47, 54 (about -2.634). Most were rejected only because the decision rule is strict.

Next: adopt a base like slot 69 or 61 (staggered-row or maximin starts). Add the slot 45 window re-solve and the slot 31 shake. Tune the restart share (15-30%). Replicate every result. Avoid more small perturbation variants and duplicate ideas.
